haemodynamics.cardiac_output_source: this project's cardiac model (four-chamber time-varying elastance + Windkessel, 60.5 s resting window)
haemodynamics.renal_fraction_source: textbook magnitude (the kidneys receive about 20-25 % of cardiac output); NOT measured in this project
haemodynamics.gfr_note: the computed value follows from the declared textbook inputs and is reported as it came out. It lands on the classic textbook 125 mL/min rather than inside the 90-120 mL/min clinical eGFR range, and has NOT been adjusted to fit the latter.

pressures.renal_artery_source: mean arterial pressure computed by this project's cardiac model, not a textbook value
pressures.pressure_source: textbook ranges for the human glomerular circuit; NOT measured in this project and NOT measured on this subject
pressures.why_it_matters: the glomerular capillary runs at roughly three times the pressure of an ordinary systemic capillary. That is not an accident of plumbing: the efferent arteriole is narrower than the afferent, so a resistance sits DOWNSTREAM of the glomerular bed and holds its pressure up. This is the physical basis of glomerular filtration and it is the reason the kidney needs two capillary beds in series.

cardiac_coupling.method: renal arterial flow is driven by the cardiac model's OWN aortic pressure waveform through a resistive (Windkessel-type) coupling: Q(t) proportional to (P_Ao(t) - P_renal_vein). This is a linear resistive coupling with no inertance and no arterial compliance, so it UNDER-predicts the systolic peak that duplex Doppler measures; the shortfall is quantified in flow_report.json rather than corrected by a gain.
cardiac_coupling.source: this project's cardiac model; is_user_personal_data = false

respiration.source: carried over unchanged from this project's cardiac model, where it was fitted as the respiratory sinus arrhythmia frequency of PhysioNet nsrdb record 16265 (PUBLIC placeholder data)
respiration.excursion_source: published renal respiratory excursion during quiet breathing; NOT measured on this subject
respiration.deformation: none — the kidney is displaced by the diaphragm, not deformed; there is no per-vertex deformation in this scene

autoregulation.description: a PHENOMENOLOGICAL autoregulation curve, not a differential equation. It reproduces the published observation that renal blood flow and GFR are held nearly constant between about 80 and 180 mmHg of renal perfusion pressure. The two mechanisms named below are LABELS on that curve, not simulated: no myogenic wall-tension equation and no macula densa / tubuloglomerular feedback kinetics are solved anywhere in this project.
mechanisms_named_but_not_simulated: myogenic response of the afferent arteriole (fast, seconds)
tubuloglomerular feedback via the macula densa (slower, tens of seconds)

tubular_handling.note: the fractions below are textbook segmental reabsorption shares, used to LABEL the nephron view. No transport equations are solved and no solute concentrations are computed anywhere in this project.
tubular_handling.source: textbook fractional reabsorption of filtered sodium and water

clinical_use: research simulator — NOT for clinical dosing or diagnosis
